title: Silver and gold have I none (Acts 3)
word: Silver and gold have I none
hook: the lame man walks and leaps into the temple
tomorrow: two fishermen face the council. why can't they stop talking?

segments.voice: Last week ended at a table: all things in common, eaten with gladness. This week starts at a gate.

At a red light, someone holds out a cup, and your hand goes to the cup holder for coins, or it doesn't. Peter and John are walking up to the temple at the hour of prayer. At "the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful" sits a man who has never walked, carried there day after day to ask for alms. He asks them. Peter has no money. So he gives something else, and it starts with his eyes.
screen: `A CUP AT A RED LIGHT.` → `THE GATE CALLED BEAUTIFUL.` → `NO MONEY. NOW WHAT?`

segments.voice: Peter stops, and he looks. "And Peter, fastening his eyes upon him with John, said, Look on us." The man looks up, "expecting to receive something of them." Then the line: "Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk." Such as I have. Peter can't give what he doesn't have, and he doesn't pretend to. Then a hand: "he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up: and immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength." And the man doesn't stroll in politely. "He leaping up stood, and walked, and entered with them into the temple, walking, and leaping, and praising God." One to tell a friend tonight: the man who sat outside the gate every day is now inside it, and loud. A crowd runs together, staring, and Peter turns the stare away from himself: "why look ye so earnestly on us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made this man to walk?" He points them to Jesus' name instead. The gift was never Peter's to show off; it was his to hand on. And it began with the cheapest thing anyone has to give: a long, straight look.
screen: `LOOK ON US.` · `SUCH AS I HAVE GIVE I THEE.` · `A HAND, AND ANKLES THAT HOLD.` · `NOT BY OUR OWN POWER.` · then, large: `WALKING AND LEAPING.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers five things you have that cost nothing to give: a minute, a skill, a name you remember, a ride, a laugh. Pause on each one as you breathe. Let the last finger rest on the one you could hand to someone this week.
Silver and gold have I none. Peter's words at the gate: no money, but what he did have, he gave.
screen: `SILVER AND GOLD HAVE I NONE — today's word`.

segments.voice: Pocket this one: walking and leaping, through the gate he used to sit outside. Day six of Acts.

howItsDone: Some Christians quote Peter's 'such as I have give I thee' when giving time or skill rather than money, and Acts 3 is read in some churches in the Easter season.

notes: The 'ninth hour' (Acts 3:1) is left as 'the hour of prayer' with no clock time, under the claims rule. 'A man who has never walked' paraphrases 'lame from his mother's womb' (3:2).
The rest of Peter's speech (Acts 3:13–26) is left out for length; it includes lines that need careful framing (3:13–15, 3:17).
'He points them to Jesus' name instead' summarizes Acts 3:16.
